rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient and mid temperature to elute all 10 compounds and map the retention window/selectivity without biasing too strongly toward either speed or resolution. All peaks are fully resolved, so the score is now limited only by runtime; the first run suggests the full elution window sits roughly between phi_e about 0.11 and 0.38, so a much narrower window with a shorter gradient should keep all compounds in-gradient while pulling the last peak toward 10 min. Keeping temperature at 40 C preserves the already-good selectivity while we test how much time can be removed without losing full resolution.

We already have full resolution, so the objective is to shave about 0.7 min from the last peak while keeping the weakest pair above 1.5. A slightly stronger, shorter gradient should move the late peak inside 10 min with only a modest loss in resolution, and phi1 0.65 gives a bit more late elution strength than simply shortening tG alone.

The 6/7 pair collapsed when the gradient was made steeper, so keep the fast 8 min format but back off to the gentler phi1=0.60 window and use a small temperature shift to probe selectivity for that specific pair. This tests whether a modest T change can recover R above 1.5 while keeping the last peak near or under 10 min.

If higher T improves that pair while retaining t_last under 10 min, it could beat the current best; if not, we will know the 10 min, 40 C method is near-optimal on temperature.

Temperature changes worsened the critical cluster, so return to 40 C and instead slightly narrow the gradient window to make the slope shallower than the failed 8 min methods. This should recover some of the 6/7 resolution while still keeping the last peak comfortably under 10 min, potentially improving on the 10 min method.

The data indicate the critical 6/7 pair is mainly slope-sensitive and worsens with temperature shifts, so the best direction is a slightly shallower gradient at 40 C. Relative to the current best, this should restore full resolution on 6/7 while only modestly increasing t_last, and it may outperform injection 2 because the narrower phi window better focuses separation where the peaks actually elute.

This directly tests whether the optimum lies at an even tighter window around the observed elution band.

The best region is clearly around phi1=0.55, tG=8, and the tradeoff suggests we need just a small selectivity improvement on the critical cluster without pushing the last peak much later. A modest cooler shift at this narrower window may open the close pair differently than it did at phi1=0.60, and if it lifts the worst R above 1.5 while keeping t_last near 10 min it can improve on the current best.

The first peak is still fairly early, so raising phi0 slightly should compress only the front of the chromatogram and may pull the last peak just under 10 min without changing the critical mid-cluster as drastically as changing temperature did. This is a targeted test of whether trimming unused low-organic space can improve time while preserving the near-best selectivity at phi1=0.55, tG=8, 40 C.
